title: delivery-log projection masks the recipient address
detail: The inline projection now masks the address with the same helper as the write path, also on rebuild, so legacy events with a full address no longer reach the attempt log. Already masked addresses and connection-name channels stay unchanged. Swallowed errors in the snapshot save, queue-depth poll and channel pre-resolve now log a scrubbed warning.

title: Package ships its event-store table catalog
detail: kumiko-es-tables.json is included in the published files; no runtime change.

title: Queued delivery jobs carry the recipient address sealed
detail: createDeliveryService takes an addressCipher; the boot wiring passes the master-key cipher, so delivery.render and delivery.send payloads hold sealedAddress instead of address. Workers open it through ctx.configEncryption.
migration: Roll out worker and web together with the same KUMIKO_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY_V<n>; a worker without the master key fails sealed jobs with send_failed. Code that calls createDeliveryService itself passes addressCipher to get sealed payloads.

title: createUnsubscribePageChromeReader gives app routes the tenant branding for unsubscribe pages
detail: The JSDoc of renderUnsubscribeResultPage pointed to a chrome read that only works for SystemAdmin, so app routes for legacy unsubscribe links rendered without branding. The new `createUnsubscribePageChromeReader({ dispatchSystemQuery })` returns `(tenantId, locale) => MailChrome | null`, failing soft to null. Build it once in the `wire` hook, whose deps now also carry `dispatchSystemQuery` (runProdApp, runWorkerApp.wireComponents, createKumikoServer), and call it with a tenant the route resolved itself, for example from the Host, never with a tenantId from the query string or body. The chrome query itself stays SystemAdmin-only; anonymous `/api/query` callers are still rejected for every tenant.

title: Unsubscribe endpoint answers form posts with an HTML page
detail: POST on the delivery unsubscribe route returns an HTML confirmation page for a form post and JSON for a bare POST. The behavior is unchanged; this only documents it.
migration: Clients that post the unsubscribe form expect HTML, API clients that post without a form content type expect JSON. No code change is needed.

title: Unsubscribe confirmation, result and link-invalid pages look like the tenant's mails
detail: The pages behind a mail's unsubscribe link now show the tenant's brand row (logo from managed-pages branding or the initial tile, name, brand suffix), the accent color, the site band and the mail footer (footer text, imprint, privacy) in a centered card with the bundled IBM Plex Sans font served same-origin, no external font CDN. Every state (confirm, unsubscribed with undo, subscribed again, failed, link invalid or expired) is translated in en, de and es and fits 375 px. The page answers with its own CSP (default-src 'none', the style block by sha256 hash, font-src 'self', img-src 'self' data: plus the logo's https origin, form-action 'self'). A browser GET or form POST with an invalid or expired token now gets a 400 HTML page instead of JSON (expired tokens keep the tenant's look and the mail's language, forged ones get the plain page in the Accept-Language language); JSON and one-click requests answer as before. Mail renderers can implement the new optional RendererPlugin.readMailChrome (renderer-mail-html does) which the system-only query delivery:query:unsubscribePageChrome reads. renderUnsubscribeResultPage takes an optional chrome and the new kind "invalid" for an app's own dead links; apps with their own CSP need style-src 'unsafe-inline' and the logo origin for it.

title: Unsubscribe links in dev and a reusable result page
detail: runDevApp accepts unsubscribe: { secret, tenantOrigin? } like runProdApp, mounts the unsubscribe routes and signs the links (base URL from auth.mail.baseUrl or APP_BASE_URL). Both share resolveUnsubscribeWiring from server-runtime. delivery exports renderUnsubscribeResultPage({ kind: "unsubscribed" | "resubscribed" | "failed", locale, resubscribeToken? }), the page the unsubscribe routes answer with, for apps that serve their own (e.g. legacy) unsubscribe links; without a resubscribeToken it offers no undo button.

title: Delivery signs unsubscribe links itself
detail: r.notification(name, { unsubscribe: true }) makes delivery put a signed data.unsubscribeUrl into every email of that notification when the service has unsubscribeLinks. User recipients get a user token, route recipients an address token (only with a blind-index key, otherwise no link). The token is scoped to tenant, notification and channel; a link the caller passes in data.unsubscribeUrl wins. runProdApp option unsubscribe: { secret } mounts createUnsubscribeRoutes and wires the links; the base URL comes from auth.publicOrigin, auth.mail.baseUrl or APP_BASE_URL, and without one boot warns and no link is added.

title: Unsubscribe links use the tenant's host and the mail's language, apps learn about address opt-outs
detail: unsubscribeLinks and the runProdApp option unsubscribe take tenantOrigin, an app callback that returns the sending tenant's own origin (subdomain or custom domain) per send; null, a throw or a non-https value fall back to the app origin and never fail the send. The signed token now carries the mail's locale (notify option locale), so the confirmation, result and undo pages render in that language; tokens without it keep working and show English. A form post to the resubscribe route now answers with an HTML page, JSON callers are unchanged. After a committed address opt-out an app job declared with trigger on DeliveryHandlers.unsubscribeAddress receives addressHash, notificationType and channel (unsubscribeAddressPayloadSchema) with the tenant in ctx.triggeredBy.tenantId; hashUnsubscribeAddress(email) matches it to the app's own subscriber. UNSUBSCRIBE_PAGE_EN exports the English page texts, German and Spanish come with the locale packages.

title: Renaming a notification type keeps user preferences and address opt-outs
detail: r.notification accepts renamedFrom, a list of former qualified names. Preferences and address opt-outs stored under a former name keep applying to the renamed notification, and a stored choice under the current name wins over one under a former name. New writes via setPreference and the unsubscribe and resubscribe handlers are stored under the current name, resubscribeAddress also lifts opt-outs under former names. Boot fails if an alias is a current notification name, is the wildcard, or is claimed by two notifications.

title: Rendered-PDF attachment variables must be JSON-serializable
detail: BigInt values or cycles in rendered-pdf variables now fail validation instead of throwing a TypeError that a retrying job hits again.

title: Delivery checks opt-outs for addresses resolved on the retry path and logs idempotency release failures
detail: The kill switch, preference and rate-limit result per recipient channel is computed once in the prefetch and reused when delivering; the rate limit now runs before the address is resolved. When the prefetch resolve failed and the address is resolved again, the suppression list is reloaded for exactly that address, so an unsubscribed address no longer receives the mail. A failing idempotency-key release is logged and swallowed instead of masking the delivery outcome.

title: A failed final delivery attempt frees the idempotency key
detail: A soft send failure and any error thrown on the final render or send attempt release the idempotency key, so the caller's retry is not dropped as a duplicate.

title: A mail without a readable inline image is sent without it
detail: An inline image whose bytes could not be read (for example a system template logo while the job context has no provider resolver) failed the whole mail send. The attachment reader now logs a warning with the fileRef id and skips the image.

title: Delivery exports the envelope-key filter for mail variables
detail: withoutDeliveryEnvelopeKeys strips reserved delivery keys from template variables.

title: NotificationRenderer and RendererInput removed, immediate notify renders with the tenant config
detail: The inline (immediate, job-less) delivery path now gets the tenant config accessor like the delivery.render job, so the mail layout shows the tenant name in both paths. DeliveryServiceOptions and CreateDeliveryTestContextOptions accept tenantConfigFor; runProdApp wires it from the boot config resolver. The types NotificationRenderer and RendererInput are removed from the delivery exports because the legacy renderer path is gone.
migration: Drop NotificationRenderer and RendererInput imports; render mails with template + meta on r.notification (see renderer-foundation).

title: ChannelContext.renderMail renders template notifications for the email channel
detail: A notification that declares a template is rendered through the mail renderer plugin with the recipient locale and the notification variables; the email channel fails when renderMail is missing instead of falling back to the legacy renderer. The job path passes the tenant config accessor to the renderer, the inline path renders without one.

title: Mails can attach a PDF that is rendered from a document template when the mail is sent
detail: notify data.attachments accepts { kind: "rendered-pdf", templateSlug, variables, fileName, locale? }. The send job renders the PDF through the document-pdf renderer, so the job payload carries the variables (at most 64000 bytes as JSON), not the bytes. Variables are stored in the job payload, so keep personal data out of them or accept that retention.

title: ChannelContext.readAttachment takes an attachment origin
detail: readAttachment(ref, origin) with origin "template" (from the renderer) or "message" (default, from notify data). Only template attachments may fall back to the system tenant; file refs from notify data stay limited to the sending tenant.

title: EMAIL_CHANNEL_NAME, createTemplateMailRenderer and createEmailAttachmentReader are exported
detail: The email channel name is a shared constant instead of a string literal. The mail renderer and the inline-attachment reader that build the channel context are exported and accept a tenant-bound db, so a handler can send through the same path as a notification.

title: Notification messages carry attachments (file refs and inline cid images)
detail: RenderedMessage and the send job payload accept attachments as references (kind file or inline), never bytes. ChannelContext.readAttachment resolves them tenant-scoped at send time; createDeliveryService takes a new filesForTenant option for the inline fallback path.

title: NotifyFactory takes an optional fileProviderResolver, so immediate and bootstrap mails can read attachments too
Queued mails render with the tenant's config again
detail: The delivery render and send jobs read the tenant config through ctx.configFor, which job contexts do not carry, so queued mails rendered without tenant name, locale, currency and branding. Both jobs now use ctx.config, which the job runner builds for the payload's tenant.

title: Delivery idempotencyKey is released when nothing was delivered
detail: A retry of a failed notify() with the same idempotencyKey is no longer skipped as a duplicate. The key is deleted when no recipient got a `sent` or `queued` delivery, also when notify() throws; one successful recipient keeps it, even if notify() throws afterwards (a retry would re-send to them). For queued channels the send/render job deletes the key after its final failed attempt, not per retry. That reference is only attached when a `route` call has exactly one channel address; `to` calls (user lists) and multi-channel routes keep the key after queueing. The job payload gains an optional `idempotencyKey`, backward compatible. `createDeliveryTestContext` accepts `idempotencyRedis`.

title: POST /resubscribe requires the undo token from the POST /unsubscribe response
migration: Clients that called the resubscribe route with the unsubscribe token must send the undo token instead: read it from the hidden token field of the page POST /unsubscribe returns (aud kumiko:resubscribe, valid for 1 hour). The unsubscribe token is rejected on /resubscribe with 400, and the undo token is rejected on /unsubscribe.

title: Delivery attempt log stores masked recipient addresses; attempts older than 90 days are pruned
detail: The log query, the export and the stored events show masked addresses, and the feature registers the daily attempt-log-retention job.
migration: Read recipients from your own data, not from the attempt log, because it only shows masked addresses now. Set `attemptLogRetentionDays` on createDeliveryFeature to another number of days, or to `false` to keep the log, if 90 days does not fit. Schedule nothing extra, the feature registers the cron job itself. Existing full-address entries are removed by the retention job once they are older than the window, or erased when their user is forgotten.

title: Forgetting a user erases the recipient address of their delivery attempts in plaintext mode too, through an event that survives projection rebuilds
Delivery log marks sends the provider did not confirm
detail: The delivery log now records when a provider accepted a send without confirming delivery (for example a Teams webhook answering 202). `store_delivery_attempts` gets a nullable boolean column `confirmed`: `false` means accepted but unconfirmed, `null` means confirmed or not applicable. The `deliveryAttempt` event carries `confirmed: false` on both the inline and the job path, `delivery:query:log` returns `confirmed` per row, and the status cell shows "Sent (unconfirmed)" for such rows.
migration: New nullable column store_delivery_attempts.confirmed. Consumers generate the migration with the generator (kumiko-schema generate) and apply it; existing rows stay null.

title: Delivery errors are fixed codes instead of raw messages
detail:
Delivery stores and returns only fixed error codes, never raw error messages. `delivery_attempts.error`, the `deliveryAttempt` event, `NotifyResult.deliveries[].error` and the job failure now hold one of `DELIVERY_FAILURE_CODES` (`timeout`, `network_error`, `redirect_blocked`, `host_not_allowed`, `missing_credentials`, `invalid_address`, `unexpected_response`, `render_failed`, `send_failed`, `channel_error`), one of `DELIVERY_SKIP_REASONS`, or `http_<status>`. A throwing channel ends as `send_failed` or `render_failed`; a failure around resolve or dispatch ends as `channel_error`. The full error goes to the log with URLs and email addresses redacted. `redactUrls` and `redactErrorText` are new next to `redactEmailAddresses`, which moved out of the step dispatcher.
`@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine` exports `DELIVERY_FAILURE_CODES`, `DELIVERY_SKIP_REASONS`, `isDeliveryErrorCode` and the types `DeliveryErrorCode`, `DeliveryFailureCode`, `DeliverySkipReason` and `ChatSendFailureCode`. `NotifyDelivery.error`, `ChannelResult.error` and `DeliveryLogEntry.error` are now `DeliveryErrorCode`. `delivery:query:log` returns `channel_error` for stored rows that still hold free text.
migration: NotifyDelivery.error is now a DeliveryErrorCode. Code that matches on error text must match the code instead (for example send_failed). Custom channels must return a DeliveryErrorCode in ChannelResult.error. Existing attempt events keep their free text; reading them through delivery:query:log masks it as channel_error.

title: Delivery log shows time and error and translates its values
detail:
The delivery log screen shows the time and the error of each attempt and translates type, channel, status and error. Error codes map to `delivery.error.<code>` (`http_<status>` to `delivery.error.http` with a `status` parameter), statuses to `delivery.status.<status>`, channels to `delivery.channel.<name>`. Every bundled channel feature registers its own channel label. Notification types are shown through `<scope>.notification.<name>` for a type `<scope>:notify:<name>`; apps register those labels, and the short name is shown when none exists. English, German and Spanish texts are included for the bundled keys.
`translateOrRaw` moved from the tenant web folder to `shared/web`; it is internal.

title: Delivery log shows the recipient name
detail: `delivery:query:log` returns a `recipientLabel` per row and the delivery log screen shows it in the recipient column: the user's display name, else the decrypted address, else the recipient id. Names are resolved with one batched lookup per page, and only when the user feature is mounted. The new `resolveUserDisplayNames(db, userIds)` is exported from the user feature. The recipient column is not sortable.

title: createDeliveryTestContext matches production notify
detail:
`createDeliveryTestContext` now behaves like the production `ctx.notify`. It takes a `secrets` option for inline-delivered chat channels and passes the calling context's job dispatcher to `notify()` on every call. Queued channels now go through the delivery jobs when the stack has a job consumer (`jobs: { consumerLane: "worker" }`); call `stack.drainJobs()` before asserting on the result. With `jobs: {}` and no `consumerLane` the attempts stay queued and `drainJobs()` never finishes. Without `jobs` they still deliver inline.
New export `createDeliveryNotifyFactory(deliveryService, { deliverQueuedInline? })` builds this `NotifyFactory` for custom setups.

title: Chat channels deliver in production boot, ctx.notify returns a NotifyResult
detail:
Chat channels (slack, discord, teams, telegram) now deliver in production boot. `runProdApp`, `runDevApp` and `runWorkerApp` pass the tenant secrets to the delivery service and hand queued channels to the `delivery.render`/`delivery.send` jobs of the calling context's job runner. `delivery.render` now receives `ctx.secrets` as well. Without a job runner, queued channels still deliver inline, now with secrets. `runBootstrap` is a one-shot process whose queue nobody drains after it exits, so it keeps delivering queued channels inline (the SystemAdmin invitation goes out before the process ends).
`NotifyFn` returns a `NotifyResult` (`{ deliveries }` with channel, recipientId, status `queued | sent | failed | skipped`, error and `deliveryAttemptId` per delivery) instead of `void`. `NotifyOptions.immediate` delivers queued channels inline for one call and bypasses job retry, for "send test message" handlers. `NotifyFactory` takes an optional job dispatcher as third argument, and `DeliveryService.notify` an optional per-call dispatcher.
Consumers: `NotifyFn` implementations in tests and mocks must now return a `NotifyResult`, e.g. `async () => ({ deliveries: [] })`. When running the API without a worker (`runSingleInstance: false`), a dedicated worker must process the delivery jobs.
migration: NotifyFn implementations in tests and mocks must return a NotifyResult, e.g. async () => ({ deliveries: [] }). Queued channels now run through the delivery jobs in production; an API-only deployment (runSingleInstance: false) needs a worker that mounts delivery and the channel features.

title: Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams and Telegram delivery channels
detail: `channel-slack`, `channel-discord`, `channel-teams` and `channel-telegram` register route-only delivery channels. Webhook URLs and the Telegram bot token live in the tenant's secrets; the send job reads them with an audit entry `<feature>:send`. `DeliveryChannel.resolve` is optional and `ChannelContext.secrets` is available on the send job path.

title: tenant broadcast recipient query no longer reads across tenants through ctx.db
detail: delivery: the `tenantUserIdsQuery` handler of a tenant broadcast now always gets a tenant-filtered `ctx.db` and `ctx.dbOutsideTransaction`, also when it is declared `r.systemScope()`. A systemScope handler could previously read the memberships of every tenant through `ctx.db` and notify users of foreign tenants. Cross-tenant reads stay available through `ctx.systemDb`.
migration: No action needed for handlers that resolve recipients through `ctx.systemDb`, like `tenant:query:resolveUserIds`. A systemScope handler that read `ctx.db` unfiltered now sees only the broadcast tenant's rows.

title: Delivery log paging no longer skips rows tied on the sort value
detail: The delivery log query no longer skips rows at a page boundary when the sort column has duplicate values. A toggle flip received while the initial snapshot loads is no longer overwritten by the older DB read. The stale job-run sweep encrypts and updates once per triggering user instead of once per run.

title: Channel plugin guard validates mode and render
detail: Stricter input guards. A delivery channel plugin must declare `mode` as `inline` or `queued` and a function `render`, otherwise boot fails instead of silently dispatching inline. The derivatives-sharp overlay rejects a non-finite `marginPct` before it reaches sharp. A document-ingest provider can no longer register under the reserved name `unknown`, which marks upcast legacy ingest events. The unsubscribe POST route also accepts a JSON body.
migration: A delivery channel plugin must now declare `mode` as `"inline"` or `"queued"` and a function `render`; boot fails otherwise instead of dispatching inline.

title: store_delivery_attempts gets an index on (tenant_id, created_at) (fw#3396)
detail: Windowed per-tenant dashboard aggregates over delivery attempts (metrics feature) filter on tenant_id and created_at.
migration: Run `kumiko migrate generate` and apply the migration: it adds `store_delivery_attempts_tenant_id_created_at_idx`.

title: New POST /api/delivery/resubscribe route undoes an unsubscribe/opt-out
detail: createUnsubscribeRoutes now also mounts POST /api/delivery/resubscribe (JSON {token} or form body only, never the query string, to stay safe against mail-client link prefetchers). It accepts the same signed tokens as the unsubscribe routes and re-enables the preference (signed-in user) or removes the address opt-out (no-account recipient). A resubscribed address opt-out is hard-deleted; a later re-opt-out for the same address/type/channel lands on a fresh event-stream generation instead of reviving the deleted one.
migration: No action needed: the route is additive and mounted automatically wherever createUnsubscribeRoutes({ secret }) already runs. Sign resubscribe links with the same signUnsubscribeToken/signAddressUnsubscribeToken used for unsubscribe links.

title: Unsubscribe route splits into a non-writing GET confirmation page and a writing POST (RFC 8058)
detail:
`createUnsubscribeRoute({ secret })`, which mounted a single `GET` route
that wrote the opt-out as a side effect of the request, is replaced by
`createUnsubscribeRoutes({ secret })`, which returns both routes for the
same path: `GET` renders a confirmation page (`<form method="post">`) and
performs no write; `POST` performs the write, reading the token from a
form-urlencoded body first, then the query string as a fallback (so an
RFC-8058 one-click client that POSTs `token=` only in the URL still works).
Token verification and error mapping (`400 unsubscribe_token_invalid`) are
unchanged and shared between both routes.
migration:
Replace `extraRoutes: [createUnsubscribeRoute({ secret })]` with
`extraRoutes: [...createUnsubscribeRoutes({ secret })]`.

Unsubscribe links already mailed out before this upgrade now show a
confirmation page on click instead of unsubscribing immediately — the
recipient must submit the form (or a one-click mail client must POST) to
complete the opt-out. If the app rendered its own confirmation page in
front of the old GET link, it can be removed; the framework route now
covers that step.

title: delivery honors an address opt-out on sends to a user account
detail:
`deliverToUser` only checked the user's notification preferences, so an
address that had been opted out via an address unsubscribe token still got
mail once it belonged to a user account. It now runs the same check
`deliverDirect` already applied: when the resolved channel address has a
`notification-address-opt-out` row for that tenant, notificationType and
channel, the attempt is logged as `skipped` / `unsubscribed` with
`recipientAddress: null`. Critical priority still bypasses it
(kumiko-framework#3275).

title: Delivery unsubscribe route is now mountable via extraRoutes
detail:
`createUnsubscribeRoute` previously returned a raw Hono app that needed a
`DbConnection` (`{ db, jwtSecret }`) and had to be mounted by hand with
`stack.app.route(...)`, bypassing the framework's request pipeline. It now
returns an `ExtraRouteDefinition` built via `signatureRoute`, taking only
`{ secret }`, and mounts at the fixed path `GET /api/delivery/unsubscribe?token=`
(exported as `DELIVERY_UNSUBSCRIBE_PATH`). Mount it with
`extraRoutes: [createUnsubscribeRoute({ secret: env.UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET })]`.
`signUnsubscribeToken` / `signAddressUnsubscribeToken` must sign with the
same secret. The secret must be at least 32 characters and must NOT reuse
the app's session `JWT_SECRET` — all three entry points fail fast on a
short secret.
The write itself now goes through two new SystemAdmin-only handlers,
`delivery:write:unsubscribe-address` and `delivery:write:unsubscribe-user`,
dispatched via `dispatchSystemWrite` once the route's `verify()` has proven
the token's authenticity. An invalid or expired token always responds 400
with `{ error: { code: "unsubscribe_token_invalid" } }`, never leaking the
underlying JWT-library error text.
New notification-preference and notification-address-opt-out rows get a
deterministic aggregate id derived from (tenant, user or address hash,
notificationType, channel), so concurrent clicks on the same link collide
at the event-store append and converge on one row instead of failing with
a unique or version conflict. Existing rows keep their ids.

title: delivery direct sends to a route address can now be unsubscribed via a signed link
detail:
ctx.notify(type, { route: { email } }) direct sends had no unsubscribe
path: only sends to a user account with a notification-preference row
could opt out, so a recipient with no account could never stop the mail.
Added hashUnsubscribeAddress (keyed blind-index hash of the trimmed,
lowercased address — the plaintext address never reaches the token or
the opt-out table), signAddressUnsubscribeToken (HS256 JWT, issuer
"kumiko:unsubscribe", no expiry — a leaked link can only opt one
address out of one notificationType/channel, and there is no signed-in
flow to request a fresh one), and a new notification-address-opt-out
event-sourced entity/table. createUnsubscribeRoute now accepts both the
existing user token and the new address token on the same route; the
existing signUnsubscribeToken and its JWT shape are unchanged. deliverDirect
now skips a channel (logDelivery status "skipped", error "unsubscribed", recipientAddress null)
when the destination address has an opt-out row for that tenant/
notificationType/channel, unless priority is "critical" — the same rule
user-preference suppression already follows. The lookup is skipped
entirely when no blind-index key is configured.
migration: Run `kumiko migrate generate` to add the notification address opt-out table.

title: delivery requires tenant
migration: delivery now declares r.requires("tenant") because its delivery-log screen references tenant:tenant. Stacks that mount delivery must also mount createTenantFeature() (and its config dependency).

title: systemScope handlers get a default per-tenant+handler rate limit; delivery:preferences opts out (fw#2861).
detail: `delivery` mounts under `r.systemScope()`, so `delivery:write:set-preference`/`delivery:query:log` without their own `rateLimit` now default to `{ per: "tenant+handler", limit: 600, windowSeconds: 60 }` once an app has a `RateLimitResolver` configured (framework change, see kumiko-framework changes.json 0.271.0). `delivery:query:preferences` declares `rateLimit: { disabled: true, reason: "..." }` — it is a self-scoped read of the caller's own notification preference rows, hit on every page load, and a per-tenant bucket would throttle the whole tenant's page loads instead of just that one handler's traffic.

title: `/delivery-log` is a declarative projectionList screen (#2221).
detail: The 103-line hand-rolled `custom` screen (`delivery-log-screen.tsx`) is gone. `r.screen({ id: DELIVERY_LOG_SCREEN_ID, type: "projectionList", ... })` drives the list off `delivery:query:log`, now built on `definePagedQueryHandler` with `cursor`/`limit`/`sort`/`sortDirection` and a server-side sort whitelist (type-guarded, not an `as`-cast) covering `createdAt`/`type`/`channel`/`status` — `recipient` isn't sortable since it's PII decrypted per-row, not a column SQL can ORDER BY. Pagination is cursor-based (`pagination: "infinite"`): `deliveryAttemptsTable.id` is an event-stream aggregate id, not a sequential PK, so there's no cheap offset/COUNT(*) path. The notificationType/recipientAddress → type/recipient display-name mapping moved from the old client component into the query handler, matching the read-projection convention for declarative list screens; column i18n keys moved from the client-only bundle into the server-registered `DELIVERY_I18N` so the generic renderer can resolve them. The status column keeps one small TSX cell (`DeliveryStatusCell`, a `StatusBadge`), registered as a `columnRenderer` — that's the only surviving hand-written UI for this screen.

title: PII on custom-event payloads (#799).
detail: PII on custom-event payloads (#799). `r.defineEvent(name, schema, { piiFields: { recipientAddress: { subjectField: "recipientId" } } })` declares payload fields that are encrypted under the owning user's DEK (crypto-shredding). Enforcement lives in the low-level event-store `append()` — the single write funnel — so `ctx.appendEvent`, MSP-apply AND out-of-dispatcher writers (delivery attempt-log, jobs run-logger) are all covered; the stored event and the returned echo carry ciphertext, keeping inline projections and rebuilds identical. A null subject field (system cron runs, recipient-less attempts) stays plaintext — there is no user key to shred. Misconfigured `piiFields` (unknown field/subjectField) throw at feature-definition time. Bundled features annotated: `delivery:event:attempt`.`recipientAddress` (subject = recipientId) and `jobs` `run-started`.`payload` (subject = triggeredById); the pseudonymous fk ids stay plaintext. `delivery log.query` and `jobs list/details` decrypt for display — a forgotten subject shows `[[erased]]`. This makes the events-only aggregates from #797 Art.-17-capable: user-forget erases the DEK, historical delivery addresses and job payloads become unreadable without touching the append-only stream. New exports: `encryptPiiValueForSubject`, `configureEventPiiCatalog`/`configuredEventPiiCatalog`/`encryptEventPayloadPii` (framework/crypto).
